Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

weightedsurv 0.2.0

Changes in behaviour

  • Input checks (KM_diff(), df_counting(), plotKM.band_subgroups()): missing values in the time, event, treatment, weight or strata column, non-finite or negative times, negative weights, a missing column (including strata.name and weight.name) and an empty treatment arm are now errors that name the column or arm (and the subgroup in plotKM.band_subgroups()). Before, some of these dropped into cryptic errors and some gave wrong results without a warning (NA survival for an NA weight, curves from negative weights or negative times). Rows are never dropped silently. The event column may be 0/1, logical, or 1/2 as survival::Surv() reads it, in all three functions (before, KM_diff() rejected 1/2). Zero weights are allowed: in df_counting() those rows no longer cause a false “Discrepancy in KM curve fit” warning, and the Cox model and log-rank test are fitted on the positive-weight rows (before, coxph() stopped on zero weights). On degenerate data (an arm without events, no events at all, one subject per arm) df_counting() now returns a result; quantities that cannot be computed (for example the hazard ratio when an arm has no events) are NA, with one warning that says why. In a stratified analysis a stratum in which one arm is empty contributes nothing (that arm’s stratum curve is NA, with the same single warning) instead of stopping the call. plotKM.band_subgroups() asks for Maxtau when an arm has no events. cox_rhogamma() warns when an arm has no events (the estimate is not finite). (B4)

  • KM_diff() returns the Kaplan-Meier value at every requested time point, whatever at_points holds. With modify_tau = TRUE, with a user grid that omits event times, and through plotKM.band_subgroups(modify_tau = TRUE), the curves, differences, variances, resampled processes and bands now equal the Kaplan-Meier estimate at those points; before they could be far off (errors above 0.4 and negative survival were seen). at_points must now be numeric, finite and non-decreasing (unsorted points used to give values outside [0, 1]). With the default grid, and in df_counting(), nothing changes. (B1)

  • Quantiles (km_quantile(), kmq_calculations(), df_counting()$quantile_results) now equal quantile(survfit(...), probs = 1 - qprob): when the curve equals the level on an interval the midpoint is returned (before, the left end; for example a median of 5.0 is now 5.5), a plateau at the level that runs to the end of follow-up is handled as survfit() does, and the confidence limits are read the same way when the limit curve is not monotone. qprob keeps its meaning, the time at which survival drops to qprob, and is documented. df_counting()$quantile_check now asks survfit() for the same quantity (probs = 1 - qprob, at conf_level); a real discrepancy is a warning even when verbose = FALSE. (B3)

  • KM_diff(): the simultaneous-band critical value is the 1 - alpha quantile (it was always the 0.95 quantile); results at alpha = 0.05 are unchanged. wlr_dhat_estimates() uses the pooled survival at tzero (it used the next grid point), so sig2_dhat and cov_wlr_dhat change slightly (by 0-8% on the test datasets; the correlation is unchanged); tzero before the first time point gives a difference of 0, and after the last time point the values there (before, an empty result). Magirr-Burman weights with mb_tstar at or beyond the last time point now use the survival at the last time point (before, all weights were 1, or infinite where survival was 0). (B5)

  • The Kaplan-Meier plots (plot_weighted_km(), KM_plot_2sample_weighted_counting(), plot_km_curves_counting()) now draw each curve from time zero at S = 1, as a step function identical to survfit()’s, and the confidence band as a step band that stays at or below 1 and closes onto the curve where survival reaches 0. Before, each curve started at its first event (the first drop and the line under early censoring marks were missing) and the band joined the event times with straight lines and could rise above 1. Everything else on the plot is unchanged. (B10)

  • Functions that draw random numbers (KM_diff() with draws or draws.band, df_counting() and calculate_risk_event_counts() with draws, cox_rhogamma() with draws) no longer reset the random-number stream of the calling session; results for a given seedstart are unchanged. (B6)

  • Weighted standard errors: when the weights are not all equal, the standard error of a weighted Kaplan-Meier curve is now the robust (infinitesimal-jackknife) standard error, S(t)^2 * sum_i w_i^2 psi_i(t)^2 with psi_i subject i’s influence contribution, in df_counting(), KM_diff() and calculate_risk_event_counts(). It equals the standard error of survival::survfit(weights = w, robust = TRUE). Every weighted standard error changes, and with it everything computed from one: pointwise limits, simultaneous-band limits and critical values, the standardised resampled curves, and the confidence limits of weighted quantiles. Unweighted results do not change, and neither do results with all weights equal (both use Greenwood’s formula; all weights equal to a constant give the unweighted standard error, where in 0.1.0 a constant weight c gave the standard error of the data with every row repeated c times). Survival estimates, differences, risk tables and the RMST point estimate do not change (the log-rank test and Cox estimate with subject weights change separately, see L1-L4 below). The standard error does not depend on the scale of the weights (weights w and 10 * w give the same answer), so weights are not frequency weights: a weight of 2 is not two copies of the row. By default weights are treated as fixed and known; for weights estimated by a logistic propensity model see weight_variance = "estimated" below. With extreme weights (low effective sample size) the standard error can be too small. (M, R1)

  • Weighted resampling: when the weights are not all equal, resampled Kaplan-Meier curves are now built from the same per-subject influence contributions, -S(t) * sum_i G_i w_i psi_i(t) for the same standard-normal multipliers G_i as before (before, the multipliers perturbed the events only). This applies to resampling_survival(), the resampled curves of KM_diff() (surv0_star, surv1_star, dhat_star, Zdhat_star), and the draws > 0 variance of KM_diff(), df_counting() and calculate_risk_event_counts(). Weighted simultaneous bands and weighted RMST bands change (cumulative_rmst_bands(): the RMST variance, pointwise limits, critical value and band limits; not the RMST estimate), and the resampling variance now agrees with the robust standard error. Unweighted results, and results with all weights equal, do not change: they keep the events-only perturbation, with the same seeds and draws. (R2)

  • Log-rank test with subject weights: when the subject weights are not all equal, the variance of the weighted log-rank score is now the sum of squared per-subject score contributions, sum_i psi_i(0)^2 (the formula is in ?df_counting), in df_counting() (unstratified and per stratum) and in wlr_cumulative() when it is given a df_counting() result. For Fleming-Harrington (0, 0) weights the z-score squared is the robust score test of survival::coxph(weights = w, robust = TRUE, ties = "breslow"). z-scores and p-values of subject-weighted log-rank tests change (z.score, sig2_lr, get_score, zlogrank_text, z.score_stratified, sig2_lr_stratified; the cumulative sig2.score and z.score of wlr_cumulative()); the score itself (lr, score, lr_stratified) does not. They no longer depend on how the weights are scaled: w, 10 * w and w / sum(w) give the same z-score (before, multiplying the weights by 10 multiplied z by about 3.2, and normalised weights gave NaN). Unweighted results, and results with all weights equal, do not change. wlr_cumulative() on a bare table of counts (no subject-level data) is unchanged too. By default weights are treated as fixed and known; for weights estimated by a logistic propensity model see weight_variance = "estimated" below. With extreme weights (low effective sample size) the test can reject too often. (L1)

  • cox_rhogamma() with subject weights: when the weights are not all equal, the standard error of the log hazard ratio is now sqrt(sum_i psi_i(bhat)^2) / i_bhat, from the same per-subject score contributions; for Fleming-Harrington (0, 0) weights it is the robust standard error of survival::coxph(weights = w, robust = TRUE, ties = "breslow"). Standard errors, confidence intervals, z-scores and p-values of subject-weighted fits change (fit$sig_bhat_asy, hr_ci_asy, cox_text_asy, fit$sig2_score, fit$z.score, zlogrank_text, and sig2_score and sig2_beta_asy of cox_score_rhogamma(score_only = FALSE)), and no longer depend on how the weights are scaled. The estimate (bhat), the scores (u.beta, u.zero), the information and the time weights do not change. Unweighted fits, and fits with all weights equal, do not change. (L2)

  • cox_rhogamma(draws > 0) with subject weights: when the weights are not all equal, the resampled scores of cox_rhogamma_resample() are now -sum_i G_i psi_i(bhat) and -sum_i G_i psi_i(0), built from the same per-subject contributions with the same multipliers G_i as before (before, the multipliers perturbed the events only). The resampling standard error, the de-biased estimate and the resampling interval of subject-weighted fits change (fit_resamples, fit$sig_bhat_star, fit$bhat_debiased, fit$wald_debiased1, fit$wald_debiased2, hr_ci_star, sig2_score_star, z.score_debiased, cox_text_star); the resampling standard error now agrees with sig_bhat_asy. Unweighted fits, and fits with all weights equal, do not change, with the same seeds and draws. (L3)

  • wlr_dhat_estimates() with subject weights: on a df_counting() result whose weights are not all equal, the variance of the log-rank statistic (as L1), the variance of the survival difference at tzero and their covariance are now computed from the same per-subject contributions; sig2_dhat equals KM_diff(draws = 0)$sig2_dhat at that time point. sig2.score, z.score, sig2_dhat, cov_wlr_dhat and cor_wlr_dhat of subject-weighted calls change; score and dhat do not. Unweighted results, and results with all weights equal, do not change. (L4)

  • plotKM.band_subgroups(): the default of draws is now 0 (it was 20). With weights that are not all equal and draws not supplied, the pointwise standard error, the pointwise limits and the standardisation of the simultaneous band now use the analytic (robust) variance instead of a variance from 20 resampling draws, so weighted band plots that do not pass draws change. Plots without weights, or with all weights equal, are numerically unaffected. Pass draws = 20 for the earlier behaviour. (B12)

  • cumulative_rmst_bands() has a new last argument mean_rule. The default, "trapezoid", gives the same results as before. "rectangle" integrates the survival difference as a step function; it then equals the difference of survfit()’s restricted means whenever the time grid holds every event time (as the default KM_diff() grid does; not with modify_tau = TRUE). The result gains an element mean_rule. (B8)

  • KM_diff() no longer plots the resampled difference curves by default (show_resamples = FALSE); use show_resamples = TRUE to see them. Results are unchanged. (B9)

  • The two confidence bands of the Kaplan-Meier plots (plot_weighted_km(), KM_plot_2sample_weighted_counting(), plot_km_curves_counting()) are now semi-transparent, in the same colours, so each stays visible where they overlap. Nothing else on the plot changes. (B11)

  • New option for estimated weights. ps_weights() (new export) fits a logistic propensity model, or takes a fitted one, and returns inverse-probability or stabilised weights together with the influence of the model’s coefficients and the derivative of each weight. Passed as weight_model with weight_variance = "estimated" to df_counting(), KM_diff(), cumulative_rmst_bands() or plotKM.band_subgroups() (two new last arguments), it carries the estimation of the weights into the Kaplan-Meier standard errors, the variance of the survival difference (no longer the sum of the arm variances), the simultaneous band, the RMST variance and band, the log-rank z-score (stratified too), logrank_results, cox_results$score, $se, $hr_ci and $pval; cox_rhogamma(), wlr_cumulative() and wlr_dhat_estimates() take the option from the df_counting() result they are given. The default is weight_variance = "known": a call that does not ask for "estimated" returns what it returned before. No estimate changes under either option. "estimated" needs a logistic glm fitted on exactly the rows analysed (subgroup analyses that reuse full-sample weights must use "known") and draws = 0; see the section “Estimated weights” of ?df_counting. Results gain an element weight_variance. (W1-W4)

  • Zero weights: whether the weights are “all equal” is now decided on the positive weights. Calls whose weight column contains a zero change: a 0/1 weight column now gives the variances, z-scores and intervals of the positive-weight rows analysed without weights (before, the zeros made the weights count as unequal and the robust formulas ran; for example a log-rank z of -0.7569 against -0.7554 for the same rows without weights). With zeros among unequal positive weights the results are those of the positive-weight rows with the same weights, as before. Resampled quantities keep a multiplier per row and are not equal to the subset’s draw by draw. Calls without a zero weight do not change. (Rd)

  • df_counting() with subject weights: logrank_results and cox_results$score are now robust tests of the weighted analysis. Calls whose positive weights are not all equal change in these two outputs only: logrank_results is the robust score test at 0 of the weighted Cox model (before, an unweighted survdiff() test that ignored the weights), and cox_results$score is summary(cox_fit)$robscore (before, the model-based score test, which reads the weights as counts). With subject weights logrank_results is the rho = 0 test whatever the scheme. check_results() now agrees on weighted Fleming-Harrington (0, 0) results instead of warning. New elements logrank_results$method ("survdiff" or "coxph_robust_score") and cox_results$se (the standard error of the log hazard ratio behind hr_ci and pval). Without weights, and with all positive weights equal, both outputs are unchanged. (Rb)

  • plotKM.band_subgroups(): the default of draws.band is now 1000 (it was 20), so the critical value of the simultaneous band no longer rests on 20 draws. Calls that do not pass draws.band change in the band (critical value, band limits, resampled curves); pointwise limits and estimates do not. Calls that pass draws.band are unchanged; pass draws.band = 20 for the earlier behaviour. (Rc)

  • df_counting() returns a new element ess: by arm, the number of rows with positive weight, the effective sample size (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) and their ratio. A low ratio means a few subjects carry most of the weight; standard errors, intervals and tests can then be too optimistic. No existing element changes and no warning depends on it. (Ra)

  • ps_weights() has the arguments formula and data (the logistic propensity model is fitted by glm()), model (a fitted logistic glm, in place of formula and data) and type = c("ipw", "stabilized"). The result has class "ps_weights" with a print() method (print.ps_weights()) that shows, by arm, the number of subjects, the smallest and largest weight, the effective sample size and its ratio to the number of subjects.

Bug fixes

  • Stratified df_counting() no longer depends on survival being attached or recent enough to find strata(). (B7)

  • Weighted Kaplan-Meier curves that end on an event now end at exactly 0. Before, a residue of about 1e-17, sometimes negative, made plot_weighted_km() stop with “values outside [0,1]” and gave “NaNs produced” warnings. Confidence limits are NA where survival is 0 (as in survfit()), and the plotted band no longer receives NaN. (B2)

  • wlr_dhat_estimates() and wlr_cumulative() with scheme = "schemper" now check for the censoring curve and say what is missing; cumulative_rmst_bands() says that it needs a KM_diff() fit made with draws.band > 0; KM_diff(draws.band < 20, show_resamples = TRUE) no longer fails; get_validated_weights() no longer prints to the console. (B5, B4, B6)

  • Internal tidying with no change in results: a local function inside df_counting() no longer shadows the exported check_km_curve(), and unused code was removed. (V)

Documentation

  • The vignettes and articles were revised for 0.2.0: the Rotterdam example now uses postmenopausal women without chemotherapy and ps_weights() with weight_variance = "estimated"; effective sample size tables were added; a new article gives the statistical details of estimated weights.
  • Vignette chunks that use a suggested package run only when it is installed; website-only packages are listed in Config/Needs/website.
